GoalGate is built with these open-source components. Tap one to read its licence.
Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and other app names shown in GoalGate are trademarks of their owners. GoalGate is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.
GoalGate does not collect, upload or share any personal information. Everything it records stays on your phone.
What GoalGate stores on your phone

Your goals, their optional \"why\" lines and steps, exactly as you typed them, when each goal applies, and when you checked off a step or marked a goal achieved; the apps you choose; and, each time the pause appears: the app\'s name, the time, how long the pause took to appear, which goal you picked (or none), your answer (Yes, Maybe, No, or downtime with its length), which reflection line was shown, and whether you chose Close or Continue; and your settings, including your workday and downtime hours. This is kept in GoalGate\'s private storage, which other apps cannot read.

To know when you open a chosen app, GoalGate reads the name of the app in front, using Android\'s usage access or accessibility service (you choose which in Settings). It never reads what is on your screen, what you type in other apps, your messages or your passwords.
Nothing. GoalGate has no internet permission, no account, no advertising, no analytics and no third-party services. Android backup is turned off for GoalGate, so its data is not copied to the cloud.
Settings > Reset GoalGate deletes your goals, records and settings. Uninstalling GoalGate deletes everything it stored.
GoalGate collects no personal information from anyone, including children.
If this policy changes, the new version will appear in the app with a new effective date.

When you open an app you chose, GoalGate shows your goals first. Tap the one you\'re working on, answer one question about the app, then tap Close to go to your home screen, or Continue to open the app. GoalGate never blocks an app.

Write up to five goals in the Goals tab, each up to 60 characters, with an optional one-line \"why\". GoalGate shows them exactly as you wrote them. Mark a goal Workday to see it only during your workday (Settings > Workday). A goal can also list steps in order: the first one not yet done appears with the goal, and you check it off in the Goals tab. Use the arrows to change the order, Edit to change or delete a goal, and Achieved when you reach one.
Open the Apps tab and switch on the apps that should start with a pause. You can change this at any time.

First, tap the goal you\'re working on, or None right now. Then you see that goal on its own, the app\'s name, and one question that asks whether opening the app helps this goal. If you tap None right now, the question changes to what you are opening the app for, with answers to match: something specific, not sure, or habit, boredom or avoiding something.

There is no wrong answer, and No never blocks the app. After you answer, a short line appears that fits your answer. In Settings > Tone you can choose how it speaks: Gentle or Direct. Settings > Reflection lines can add a Korean version.

On the pause, tap It\'s my downtime, then choose 15, 30 or 60 minutes. Continue opens the app with no wait, and GoalGate leaves all your chosen apps alone for that time. If you are still in a chosen app when the time is up, one check asks whether to keep going. In Settings > Downtime you can set daily downtime hours, weekends and public holidays; at those times, It\'s my downtime comes first.
Close takes you to the home screen. Continue opens the app. If you open the same app 3 times within an hour, Continue waits 5 seconds (10 seconds from the 5th time). Close always works straight away.
After you continue to an app, GoalGate does not ask again for that app for 1, 5 or 15 minutes. Change it in Settings > Cooldown.

Optional. If you keep using an app for 5, 15 or 30 minutes after continuing, GoalGate pauses you again. Leaving the app for less than a minute does not reset the clock. Turn it on in Settings > Time check.

The Reflections tab shows the last seven days: how often you answered Yes, Maybe and No, which goals you picked, how often you chose Close, and each app\'s week. One sentence sums up the week. There are no scores and no streaks.

Touch and hold an empty part of your home screen, tap Widgets, then choose GoalGate. It shows the goal you picked most recently today, or your first goal if you haven\'t picked one yet. Tap Check in to open the Goals tab.

Engine A (usage access) works on every phone and shows a permanent, silent notification. Engine B (accessibility) is usually faster. Switch in Settings > Detection engine. The permissions each engine needs are listed below it.

1. In Settings, check that every item under Permissions for this engine shows Done.\n2. On Samsung phones, go to Settings > Battery > Background usage limits > Never sleeping apps and add GoalGate.\n3. If the Engine B switch is greyed out, follow the steps shown under the accessibility permission in Settings.
Settings > Reset GoalGate deletes your goals, records and settings and starts setup again. Permissions you allowed stay on, so setup skips those steps.
GoalGate has no account and no internet access. Your goals, answers and reflections stay on this phone. Uninstalling GoalGate deletes all of it.
GoalGate speaks English and Korean. In Settings > Language, choose one for GoalGate alone, or choose System to follow your phone. Settings > Theme works the same way for Light and Dark.

Stops Android from putting GoalGate to sleep. On Samsung, also add GoalGate to \"Never sleeping apps\".

GoalGate uses Android\'s Accessibility API only to notice when you open one of the apps you chose, so it can show your goals and the pause.
Only the name of the app that is in front, for example \"Instagram\".
It never reads what is on your screen: messages, passwords, typing, or anything else inside your apps. The service is built without access to screen content.
The app name stays on this phone. GoalGate has no internet access, so it cannot send anything anywhere. You can turn the service off at any time in Android settings.
GoalGate uses this service only to see which app is in front, so it can show your goals when you open an app you chose. It does not read anything on your screen, and no data leaves your phone.
